title: GBS-MeDIP: A protocol for parallel identification of genetic and epigenetic variation
author: Rezaei, Uffenorde, et al.
materials: DNA samples are extracted with Qiagen DNeasy blood and tissue kit (Cat. No. 69504) or any other high-quality DNA extraction kit according to the manufacturer's protocol.1.Follow the protocol of Qiagen Dneasy blood and tissue kit.2.Measure the DNA concentration of the samples using Qubit fluorimeter and perform the necessary dilutions to obtain a minimum final concentration of 15 ng/μL.Pause point: isolated DNA can be stored at −20°C for use in subsequent steps.Note: Run the DNA samples on 1% agarose gel electrophoresis to verify the integrity of the extracted DNA.CRITICAL: It is recommended to use the Qubit™ Fluorometric DNA Quantification system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to measure the DNA concentration, and nanodrop to check purity (a ratio of absorbance at 260 nm vs 280 nm of ∼1.8 is considered optimal). To prepare the Qubit™ reagents, follow the instruction of its kit. It is recommended to consider the results of Qubit™ measurements as the basis for calculating the amount of DNA. The concentrations measured should allow the addition of 400 ng of each individual DNA to be digested with the PstI enzyme within a reaction volume of 30 μl (see below of the detailed components of the PstI digestion reaction).

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from each sample using the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Cat. No. 69504) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Quantify and dilute DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit fluorometer (Thermo Fisher) and, if necessary, dilute samples to a minimum of 15 ng/µL; optionally check purity with a Nanodrop (260 nm/280 nm ≈ 1.8). Prepare enough DNA so that 400 ng of each sample will be used in the subsequent PstI digestion (30 µL reaction volume).

steps.title: Verify DNA integrity
steps.instruction: Run 1 µL of each extracted DNA on a 1 % agarose gel to confirm high‑molecular‑weight integrity.

steps.title: Prepare adapter stock solution
steps.instruction: Make a 3 ng/µL stock of the Illumina adapters, then dilute 1:4 with TE water to obtain a working solution of 0.6 ng/µL.

steps.title: Register barcodes and set up ligation mix
steps.instruction: Assign a barcode adapter to each sample, vortex the plate at low speed, then spin 30 s at low speed (≈21‑22 °C). In a PCR plate, combine 3 µL of the 0.6 ng/µL adapter solution with 8 µL of each PstI‑digested DNA (≈100 ng).

steps.title: Prepare ligation master mix
steps.instruction: For each reaction add up to 8 µL of DNA + adapter mixture, nuclease‑free H₂O to a final volume of 30 µL, 3 µL 10× NEB Buffer, and 1 µL NEB T4 DNA ligase (use reverse pipetting because of viscosity).

steps.title: Ligate adapters
steps.instruction: Incubate the ligation reactions for 2 h at 22 °C, then 30 min at 65 °C.

steps.title: Pool ligation reactions and purify
steps.instruction: Collect the entire 30 µL from each ligation well into a single 1.5‑ or 2‑mL tube and purify the pool with the Qiagen QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (Cat# M0202L) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Transfer pool to a 15 mL Falcon tube, add 5 volumes of PB buffer, vortex to mix.
Load ≤750 µL of the mixture onto each silica spin column (max 1.5 mL per column) and centrifuge 1 min at 10 000 × g, 21‑22 °C; discard flow‑through.
Repeat the spin with the remaining volume using the same column.
Add 750 µL PE buffer (containing 96‑100 % ethanol) to the column, centrifuge, discard flow‑through, centrifuge again to remove residual buffer.
Add 30 µL EB buffer to the column centre, incubate 1 min at 21‑22 °C, centrifuge 1 min at 10 000 × g.
Add a second 30 µL EB buffer, incubate 1 min, centrifuge 1 min at 10 000 × g.
Combine eluates from all columns into one tube.
If the volume exceeds 25 µL, concentrate with a speed‑vac at 55 °C (final volume ≤25 µL).

steps.title: Store purified library
steps.instruction: If the pool contains >50 samples, transfer each 30 µL ligation reaction directly to a 15 mL Falcon tube before purification. Store the purified library at –20 °C (short‑term) or –20 °C to –80 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Purify PCR products with magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Perform a second purification of the PCR‑amplified library using AMPure XP magnetic beads as described in step 11 of the original protocol.

steps.title: Measure purified library concentration
steps.instruction: Quantify the bead‑purified library with Qubit; the expected concentration is 3–5 ng/µL.

steps.title: Store library before sequencing
steps.instruction: Pause point: keep the purified library at –20 °C until next‑generation sequencing is performed.

steps.title: First quality‑control gel
steps.instruction: Run 1 µL of each PstI‑digested DNA sample on a 1.5 % agarose gel; a homogeneous smear indicates successful digestion, whereas high‑molecular‑weight bands indicate incomplete digestion that must be optimized.

description:
The protocol below describes the specific steps using Homo sapiens as species model, however, we have already successfully applied this protocol using Gallus
gallus (Pertille et al., 2019; Pértille et al., 2016, 2017a, 2017b, 2020), Canis familiaris (Sundman et al., 2020), Sus scrofa (Pértille et al., 2021), Macrossoma macropomum (Nunes et al., 2017, 2020), and Mus musculus (Unpublished data) species. Before starting, keep in mind to clean the bench properly and to check the list of materials, reagents, and buffers needed. The library-building pipeline involves basic laboratory skills. After DNA extraction, experienced users can complete the total workflow of our optimized procedure in 4–5 days. The method involves sequencing of the libraries in the Illumina platform, which is available at many sequencing facilities around the world. Sequencing should be performed in professional core facilities having validated instruments and experienced technicians. Bioinformatic expertise is required for later quality control and analysis of the sequencing data. This section lists the major steps and provides step-by-step details and timing for each major step.
